required_documents.details: Must be valid for the duration of your stay. Include all previous passports if available.
Apply online at gov.uk. You will receive a reference number to bring to your appointment.
You must attend a Visa Application Centre (VAC) to give fingerprints and a photo.
Shows you can financially support yourself. Minimum balance varies; typically £1,000+ recommended for a 2-week trip.
Hotel bookings, Airbnb confirmation, or invitation letter from host with their address and contact details.
Confirmed or provisional flight booking showing entry and exit dates.
Employment letter stating your position, salary, and approved leave. Or enrollment letter from school/university.
Previous visas (especially UK, US, Schengen) strengthen your application. Include copies of relevant pages.
From your UK host, including their address, immigration status, and relationship to you.
Not mandatory but strongly recommended. Should cover the full duration of stay.

application_steps: Step 1: Complete the online application form at gov.uk/standard-visitor/apply-standard-visitor-visa
Step 2: Pay the visa fee (£115 for standard processing)
Step 3: Book a biometric appointment at your nearest UK Visa Application Centre (VFS Global or TLScontact)
Step 5: Attend your biometric appointment with all documents
Step 6: Track your application online using your reference number
Step 7: Collect your passport (or receive it by post)
key_notes: You must apply from your country of residence, not your nationality country
UKVI assesses your intention to leave the UK at the end of your visit
Strong ties to your home country (job, family, property) significantly improve approval chances
Do NOT book non-refundable flights before your visa is approved
Nationals of some countries may be eligible for Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) instead

short_stay_c.authority: Embassy of the destination Schengen country
short_stay_c.processing_days: 15 calendar days (standard), up to 45 days in complex cases
short_stay_c.validity: Up to 90 days within any 180-day period
short_stay_c.which_embassy: Apply at the embassy of the country where you will spend the most days. If equal time, apply at the country of first entry.

required_documents.details: Must be valid for at least 3 months beyond your intended departure from the Schengen Area. Must have been issued within the last 10 years. Must have at least 2 blank pages.
Signed by the applicant. Available from the embassy website or VFS Global/TLScontact.
35×45mm, white background, taken within the last 6 months. Must comply with ICAO biometric standards.
Minimum coverage of €30,000. Must be valid for the entire Schengen Area and the full duration of stay. Must cover medical emergency and repatriation.
Confirmed or provisional booking showing entry and exit dates. Do NOT purchase non-refundable tickets before visa approval.
Hotel bookings, Airbnb confirmation, or invitation letter from host (with their address, contact, and copy of their ID/residence permit).
Bank statements for the last 3–6 months. Minimum recommended: €50–€100 per day of stay depending on the country. Some countries accept a sponsor's financial guarantee.
Employment letter (position, salary, approved leave dates) or enrollment letter. Self-employed: business registration + tax returns.
Explaining the purpose of your trip, itinerary, and confirmation that you will return home.

required_documents.document: Proof of ties to home country
required_documents.details: Property ownership, family ties, permanent employment contract. Strengthens your application.
Copies of previously granted visas demonstrate travel history and improve approval chances.
From your host in the Schengen country, with their address, contact, and copy of their ID or residence permit.

application_steps: Step 1: Determine which Schengen country's embassy to apply to (country of longest stay, or first entry if equal)
Step 2: Book an appointment at the relevant embassy or Visa Application Centre (VFS Global / TLScontact / BLS International)
Step 3: Complete the Schengen visa application form
Step 5: Pay the visa fee (€90 for adults)
Step 6: Attend your appointment with all original documents
Step 8: Collect your passport with the visa sticker
key_notes: You can only stay 90 days in any 180-day rolling period across ALL Schengen countries combined
Apply no earlier than 6 months before your trip and no later than 15 working days before
Biometrics (fingerprints + photo) are collected at the Visa Application Centre
Some nationalities may need to apply directly at the embassy, not a VAC
A Schengen visa does NOT guarantee entry — border officers have final authority
